rows.answer: The weight of the ResMed AirSense 11 with its standard humidifier tub is 1130 grams or 40 ounces (AirSense 11).

The operating pressure range of the DreamStation CPAP is 4-20 cmH2O (DreamStation CPAP). This pressure range is measured at the mask (Mode pressure range CPAP). When using CPAP with EPR (Expiratory Pressure Relief) mode, the pressure range remains 4-20 cmH2O, with EPR reducing the pressure during expiration by 1.0, 2.0, or 3.0 cmH2O depending on the level set, but the delivered pressure will not drop below 4.0 cmH2O (Mode pressure range CPAP).
The sound pressure level of the Resvent iBreeze CPAP is 28 dB (iBreeze CPAP System). The measurement has an uncertainty of 2 dB (iBreeze CPAP System).
The warranty period of the DreamStation CPAP device is 2 years (DreamStation CPAP). The DreamStation CPAP Pro, which is a related model, also has a warranty of 2 years (DreamStation CPAP Pro).

Based on the knowledge graph, the DreamStation CPAP has a Smart Ramp feature with a ramp time setting of 0 to 45 minutes in 5-minute increments (DreamStation CPAP Pro, Smart Ramp). The starting ramp pressure is patient adjustable (DreamStation CPAP Pro). However, the specific default ramp time value for the DreamStation CPAP is not explicitly stated in the provided context.
The maximum water capacity of the ResMed AirSense 11 humidifier tub is 380 mL (Water Capacity, AirSense 11).

The ResMed AirStart 10 is quieter than the ResMed AirSense 11. The AirStart 10 has a sound pressure level of 26.6 dBA (AirStart 10 CPAP), while the AirSense 11 has a noise level of 35 dBA (Noise Level, AirSense 11). Both measurements have an uncertainty of ±2 dBA.

On the DreamStation, SmartRamp mode differs from standard ramp mode in how it adjusts pressure. While a standard ramp uses a fixed time-based pressure increase (SmartRamp), SmartRamp maintains a constant lower pressure until the device detects that you require more pressure (Alternately, the SmartRamp mode maintains a constant lower pressure until the device detects that you require more pressure). In other words, SmartRamp is an intelligent ramp mode that automatically adjusts pressure based on patient breathing patterns (SmartRamp), rather than simply increasing pressure over a predetermined time period like the standard ramp function.

The ResMed AirSense 10 AutoSet for Her is the device that has a therapy algorithm designed specifically for women (ResMed AirSense 10 AutoSet for Her, AirSense 10 AutoSet for Her). This device features the AutoSet for Her algorithm, which is the first dedicated algorithm designed to treat obstructive sleep apnea in female patients (AutoSet for Her algorithm). The algorithm addresses the higher instances of flow limitation often seen in women with sleep apnea and is designed to detect flow limitation early to apply pressure changes steadily and comfortably throughout the night (AutoSet for Her algorithm).

The purpose of the EZ-Start feature on the DreamStation CPAP Pro is to provide automatic, personalized adjustments to CPAP pressure designed to help patients gradually acclimate to their prescribed level of therapy (EZ-Start). Specifically, EZ-Start enhances patient acclimation (EZ-Start) and provides personalized adjustments (EZ-Start) to make the therapy more comfortable and easier to adapt to for new CPAP users.

The 135-degree angle in the submersed tubing of the Seattle-PAP Bubble CPAP system accomplishes the following: it increases the amplitude of oscillations, thus providing effects similar to high frequency oscillatory ventilation for improving gas exchange and offering more efficient respiratory support compared to other methods of noninvasive respiratory support (Seattle-PAP, Pressure Oscillations, High Frequency Oscillatory Ventilation). These pressure oscillations improve gas exchange and reduce respiratory muscle work (Bubble CPAP Therapy). The vibrations from the bubbling mechanism help contribute to gas exchange and reduce the infant's work of breathing (Bubble CPAP).

The ResMed AutoRamp feature relies on sleep onset detection to know when to ramp up to the prescribed pressure (AutoRamp with sleep onset detection, AutoRamp). Specifically, AutoRamp is described as a feature with sleep onset detection that starts with low pressure and ramps up to prescribed pressure once the patient falls asleep (AutoRamp). The AutoRamp with sleep onset detection responds by comfortably ramping up to prescribed pressure the moment it detects sleep onset (AutoRamp with sleep onset detection).

On the ResMed AirSense 11, the EPR (Expiratory Pressure Relief) feature gently lowers the pressure delivered when you exhale, making it easier to breathe out against the air pressure (Expiratory pressure relief, EPR). When EPR is enabled, you may find it easier to breathe out (EPR). The feature has three levels of pressure reduction: Level 1 reduces pressure by 1.0 cmH2O, Level 2 reduces by 2.0 cmH2O, and Level 3 reduces by 3.0 cmH2O (EPR). The minimum pressure for EPR operation is 4.0 cmH2O (EPR).
